claim: In our first authoring-loop pilot (2026-08-21) a critic rule that counted sectors measured the wrong thing: a courtyard of 1,008 player areas was called 'circulation' because six tiny stair steps outnumbered it. Since then our rules weigh by floor area, express scale as a percentile among corpus sectors of comparable footprint (never a round multiple of the body), never count a skipped evaluator as a pass, and a new rule is cross-checked against a rendered frame before it is trusted.
evidence: First authoring-loop pilot, 2026-08-21: docs/history/authoring-loop.md:92-96; three iterations passed every gate while the level was an axis-aligned grid in the bottom decile for ceiling height
bloodmap/authoring_loop.py:725-747 at commit 7847923, the last that has the module (transition_regions_dominate_space fires on floor-area share, not sector count)
use: Area-weighted measures and corpus percentiles; no aggregate quality score.
